settings.title: Years serving New Rochelle & Westchester since 1980
AC Problems Our Technicians Repair

settings.editor: Different cooling problems can produce similar symptoms. Warm air may come from restricted airflow, a frozen coil, low refrigerant, an electrical failure, or a compressor issue — and a system that will not start could have a failed capacitor, damaged wiring, or another control problem. We diagnose before we repair.

settings.title: Repairs We Handle

icon_list.text: Damaged blower and condenser fan motors
Faulty wiring, switches, sensors, and controls

settings.title: Turn It Off & Call Us If You Notice

icon_list.text: Warm air, weak airflow, or uneven cooling
Frequent starts and stops or constant operation
Water or ice around the equipment
An outdoor unit that hums but will not start
Repeated breaker trips or a sudden jump in cooling costs

settings.editor: During consecutive hot, humid days in Westchester County, a struggling system may cool adequately in the morning but fall behind by afternoon — upper floors, finished attics, additions, and rooms on older ductwork feel it first. These symptoms don’t automatically mean replacement; they mean airflow, electrical components, refrigerant operation, and overall performance should be evaluated before the problem gets more extensive.

settings.title: A Repair Visit Built Around Clear Answers

settings.editor: For more than 40 years, G.C. Reliable has helped New Rochelle and Westchester County customers make sense of cooling problems without unnecessary pressure — careful testing, straightforward communication, and quality workmanship at every step.

settings.title: 01.  Your Symptoms Help Guide the Diagnosis

settings.editor: Your technician asks what you have noticed and when — weak afternoon cooling, unusual startup noises, or repeated shutdowns all help focus the inspection on the issue affecting your comfort.

settings.title: 02.  We Test Before Recommending a Repair

settings.editor: Rather than swapping the most obvious part, we evaluate the equipment and related components — electrical, airflow, controls, drainage, refrigerant, motors, coils, and overall performance — to find what actually failed.

settings.title: 03.  You Review the Findings Before Work Begins

settings.editor: We explain the findings, the proposed repair, and what the estimate includes. When more than one option is reasonable, you compare them on cost, system age, condition, efficiency, and expected reliability before deciding.

settings.title: 04.  We Use Quality Parts and Proper Methods

settings.editor: We use quality components and follow manufacturer specifications, and our trucks carry many commonly needed parts. If a specialized component must be ordered, we explain the next steps and timeline.

settings.title: 05.  We Verify Performance Before Leaving

settings.editor: After the approved repair, we test that the system starts, runs, and cools as expected, review the work, and flag any developing concerns — so you know what failed, what was fixed, and how it is performing.

settings.title: What Westchester Homeowners Ask Before Scheduling

tabs.tab_title: Does my AC need repair or maintenance?
tabs.tab_content: Repair addresses an active malfunction — warm air, leaking, unusual noises, short cycling, weak airflow, or failure to start. Maintenance is preventive service for equipment that is generally operating; a tune-up may reveal developing concerns but is not a substitute for diagnosing an existing failure. Describe the symptoms when booking so the right appointment is arranged.

tabs.tab_title: Should I repair or replace my air conditioner?
tabs.tab_content: Repair often makes sense when the system is relatively new, the problem is isolated, and the equipment has otherwise been reliable. Replacement may offer better long-term value when the AC is older, inefficient, repeatedly breaking down, or facing an expensive compressor or refrigerant-system repair.

tabs.tab_title: How much does AC repair cost?
tabs.tab_content: The price depends on the failed component, equipment type, required parts, repair complexity, and whether after-hours service is needed. Before approving service, ask whether the estimate includes diagnosis, parts, labor, system testing, and warranty coverage — we explain the work and pricing first.

tabs.tab_title: Can I keep running my AC if it is still cooling?
tabs.tab_content: Gradually weakening performance or uneven cooling may not require an immediate shutdown, but the system should still be inspected. Turn the AC off if it repeatedly trips the breaker, produces a burning smell, makes loud grinding noises, leaks near electrical components, or hums without starting.

tabs.tab_title: Do you provide emergency AC repair?
tabs.tab_content: Yes — G.C. Reliable offers 24/7 emergency HVAC service throughout New Rochelle and Westchester County, appropriate when the system stops cooling during extreme heat, shows signs of an electrical hazard, or creates indoor conditions that could affect children, older adults, pets, or people with health concerns.
